findings.body:
Step 3.5 runs **before** the release is published, so its failure takes Steps 4–5 down with it: GitHub Actions halts the job on a failed step, meaning a transient `npx skills update` error (the `sleep 5` propagation guard is optimistic) leaves the already-pushed `vX.Y.Z` tag with no GitHub Release object or notes. The `git push origin HEAD:main` below also has no pull/rebase, so a commit landing on `main` during the multi-second npm install rejects the push with the same effect.

Move this step after Step 5 — the release publish consumes nothing it produces — and add `git pull --rebase --autostash origin main` before committing. The PR's risk note ("the tag itself is already published even if 3.5 fails") undercounts the blast radius: Steps 4–5 are skipped too.

This is the first workflow step in the repo that executes an npm package at run time, and `npx --yes skills` resolves to whatever is latest on npm at that moment — a compromised or maliciously updated `skills` release would execute on this runner holding a token that can push to `main` (`permissions: contents: write`; the checkout at line 43 uses `AUTOMATION_GITHUB_TOKEN || GITHUB_TOKEN`). That's arbitrary code execution in the release path of an action thousands of consumers pin.

Pin the CLI the same way third-party actions are SHA-pinned: `npx --yes skills@<version> update ai-diff-reviewer`, bumped deliberately in a reviewed change. The smoke-test value is unaffected — the skill *content* still installs exactly as a consumer's would. (Verified: no other workflow under `.github/workflows/` runs `npx` today, so this is a new surface, not an existing pattern.)

If tag propagation lags past the `sleep 5`, `npx skills update` can resolve the *previous* tag, change nothing, and this line then claims the vendored copy is "already at ${NEW_VERSION}" while it is actually still on the prior release — misleading precisely during the lag scenario this step is built around.

Derive the message from the installed version (e.g. `grep '^version:' .agents/skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md`) instead of asserting the expected one.

summary:
## Verdict

Solid, well-evidenced dogfooding work — the vendoring is byte-consistent and every code-anchored claim in the new `.review/extension.md` verifies against the codebase — but the new `auto-release.yml` step sits **before** release publication (so its failure suppresses release notes), and it introduces an unpinned npm-execution surface into the release path.

## Findings

| # | Severity | File | Summary |
|---|----------|------|---------|
| 1 | ⚠️ warning  | `.github/workflows/auto-release.yml:191` | Step 3.5 failure skips Steps 4–5 — pushed tag ends up with no GitHub Release or notes |
| 2 | ⚠️ warning  | `.github/workflows/auto-release.yml:206` | `npx --yes skills` is unpinned and executes on a runner holding a `main`-pushing token |
| 3 | ℹ️ info     | `.github/workflows/auto-release.yml:210` | "already at ${NEW_VERSION}" message can be wrong during tag-propagation lag |

## What didn't fit in inline comments

**Parity verification — all green.** `diff -rq .agents/skills/ai-diff-reviewer skills/ai-diff-reviewer` → byte-identical; both `prompt.md` copies are byte-identical to `prompts/default.md` (the CI prompt-sync invariant holds); all three SKILL.md `version:` fields agree at 1.4.2 between vendored and source-of-truth copies.

**The `[skip release]` loop-guard is sound.** The job-level `if` (`.github/workflows/auto-release.yml:35-37`) catches both the `chore(release):` prefix and the `[skip release]` marker, so Step 3.5's own push to `main` cannot re-trigger the workflow. The Step 2.5 → 3 → 3.5 sequencing (bump version → tag → refresh vendored from the fresh tag) is coherent.

**`.review/extension.md` fact-check — every claim resolves.** `scripts/reviewer.py` is 4018 LOC ("~4000" ✓); `MAX_TOOL_OUTPUT_BYTES: int = 32_000`, `DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS: int = 30`, and `SEVERITY_CRITICAL: str = "critical"` exist verbatim; every named helper (`safe_repo_path`, `_build_cli_env`, `_CLI_ENV_ALLOWLIST`, `run_cmd`, `redact_for_log`, `register_secret`/`scrub_secrets`, `w
